title: How to Refresh DNS and Restart Windows
overview: Use this article to perform the VPN workflow's bounded DNS refresh. It clears only the local Windows DNS resolver cache with ipconfig /flushdns, then restarts Windows and retests the VPN. It does not reset Winsock or TCP/IP and does not release or renew network addressing.
checklist: Save open work and disconnect the VPN client.
On a managed device, follow your organization's approved procedure before opening an elevated Command Prompt or changing network state.
Open Command Prompt and run only ipconfig /flushdns for this workflow step.
Confirm that Windows reports the DNS resolver cache was flushed.
Restart Windows, reconnect to the normal network, and retry the VPN connection.
Record whether the VPN connected and return to the workflow before making another change.
Do not run netsh resets or ipconfig /release or /renew unless an IT administrator or the VPN provider's official instructions explicitly require them.
common_indicators: The VPN still does not connect after the client, computer, security software, and adapter checks.
A stale local DNS resolver entry may be affecting access to the VPN service.
The workflow has reached Refresh DNS and Restart Windows.

commands.description: Clears the local Windows DNS resolver cache without resetting Winsock, TCP/IP, DHCP leases, or managed network configuration.

quiz.question: Which command is authorized by this workflow step?

notes: Safety correction aligns the article with the active workflow's bounded ipconfig /flushdns action.
Broad network-reset and DHCP lease commands were removed because they can interrupt connectivity or alter managed configuration.
